proposed.title: Normalize OS errors during ZoneInfo validation
answers: Why does an invalid timezone raise an OS error instead of a validation error?
How should ZoneInfo constructor failures be reported?
How are overly long timezone names validated?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Invalid timezone inputs such as 'America' or a 300-character name raise an OS error instead of a ValidationError.
Root cause: pydantic/_internal/_validators.py:validate_str_is_valid_iana_tz did not catch OSError from ZoneInfo(value).
Fix pattern: Translate ZoneInfoNotFoundError, ValueError, TypeError and OSError into PydanticCustomError with type 'zoneinfo_str', message 'invalid timezone: {value}' and the original value in context; regression coverage is in tests/types/test_zoneinfo.py:test_zoneinfo_os_error_is_validation_error.
Constraints: This normalization applies to ZoneInfo construction during validation; existing ZoneInfo instances pass through, and exceptions outside the listed set are not caught.
proposed.applies: Validation of ZoneInfo fields and TypeAdapter(ZoneInfo) inputs.

proposed.title: Keep legacy timedelta settings isolated during inferred serialization
answers: Why does ser_json_timedelta='float' turn datetime values into numbers?
How should TypeAdapter(Any) serialize dates and durations?
Which mode controls inferred timedelta values and dictionary keys?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Setting ser_json_timedelta='float' makes inferred datetime, date and time values serialize as numbers instead of ISO strings.
Root cause: pydantic-core/src/serializers/config.rs:SerializationConfig::from_config previously resolved one shared temporal mode using the timedelta setting.
Fix pattern: Maintain separate temporal_mode and timedelta_mode fields; use timedelta_mode for timedelta branches in pydantic-core/src/serializers/infer.rs:infer_to_python_known, infer_serialize_known and infer_json_key_known so JSON-compatible values, JSON output and dictionary keys agree.
Constraints: The legacy ser_json_timedelta setting affects only timedeltas; ser_json_temporal affects all temporal types. This separation concerns JSON serialization by inference, including unknown types such as Any.
proposed.applies: Changes to temporal configuration or inferred JSON serialization of datetime, date, time and timedelta values and keys.

proposed.title: Preserve the two timedelta precedence rules
answers: Which setting wins when ser_json_temporal and ser_json_timedelta are both supplied?
Does explicitly configuring ISO temporal output override float durations?
How do temporal_mode and timedelta_mode interact in to_jsonable_python?
proposed.body:
Invariant: Dictionary configuration gives ser_json_temporal precedence whenever the key is present, including an explicit iso8601 value; otherwise timedeltas use ser_json_timedelta.
Enforcement: pydantic-core/src/serializers/config.rs:TemporalMode::timedelta_from_config centralizes this presence check and is used by SerializationConfig::from_config and pydantic-core/src/serializers/type_serializers/timedelta.rs:TimeDeltaSerializer::build, keeping inferred and typed timedelta serialization aligned.
Argument exception: pydantic-core/src/serializers/config.rs:SerializationConfig::from_args instead uses timedelta_mode when temporal_mode equals iso8601; any other temporal_mode takes precedence for timedeltas.
Consequence: Replacing the configuration presence check with a value comparison changes explicit ISO overrides; applying the presence-based rule to argument resolution removes its default-mode fallback.
proposed.applies: Changes to timedelta mode resolution across dictionary configuration, serializer construction and direct serialization arguments.

proposed.title: Keep declared configuration separate from derived settings
answers: Why does a child model still accept field names after disabling populate_by_name?
Why did Pydantic add validation settings to my model_config?
How should internal configuration defaults be applied without changing user configuration?
proposed.body:
Symptom: A child model accepts field names despite populate_by_name=False, or model_config exposes validation settings the user never declared.
Root cause: pydantic/_internal/_config.py:ConfigWrapper.core_config formerly inserted derived settings into the declared mapping, allowing parent-derived settings to override a child's declaration.
Fix pattern: pydantic/_internal/_config.py:prepare_config copies supplied dictionaries; ConfigWrapper keeps declarations in config_dict and derives effective_config through _build_effective_config. Configuration consumers use wrapper attributes or core_config().
Constraints: config_dict is exposed as model_config or __pydantic_config__ and supplies inheritance merges, so internal normalization must never mutate it. This does not require effective_config to be a separate copy when no derived settings are needed.
proposed.applies: Configuration ownership, normalization, inheritance, and consumers of ConfigWrapper.

proposed.title: Normalize alias validation eagerly and use it for signatures
answers: How do populate_by_name and validate_by_alias interact?
Why does disabling alias validation still allow field names?
Should invalid alias settings fail with defer_build enabled?
Why does the model signature show an alias despite validate_by_alias=False?
proposed.body:
pydantic/_internal/_config.py:_build_effective_config applies compatibility settings only when validate_by_name is absent or None: a non-None populate_by_name forces validate_by_alias=True and supplies validate_by_name; otherwise validate_by_alias=False implies validate_by_name=True.
The same function rejects configurations allowing neither aliases nor names with error code validate-by-alias-and-name-false. ConfigWrapper.__init__ enforces this before schema building, including deferred builds and unresolved annotations.
Explicit non-None validate_by_name bypasses these derivations; preserve that precedence when changing configuration normalization.
Model and dataclass signature generation receive effective validate_by_alias through pydantic/_internal/_model_construction.py:complete_model_class and pydantic/_internal/_dataclasses.py:complete_dataclass; pydantic/_internal/_signature.py:generate_pydantic_signature does not take validate_by_name.
Skipping effective configuration when generating signatures can make the displayed constructor parameters disagree with the compatibility settings used for validation.
proposed.applies: Alias/name validation configuration and generated model or dataclass signatures.

proposed.title: Emit schema_generator deprecation warnings during configuration preparation
answers: Where should the schema_generator deprecation warning be emitted?
Why are schema_generator warnings repeated during schema construction?
Does the schema_generator configuration setting still affect validation?
proposed.body:
pydantic/_internal/_config.py:check_deprecated warns when schema_generator is non-None; prepare_config invokes this check during configuration preparation.
Keep this warning out of ConfigWrapper.core_config: the notice belongs to configuration preparation, rather than each core configuration build, which can repeat it.
pydantic/config.py:ConfigDict documents that schema_generator no longer has any effect; pydantic/_internal/_config.py:check_deprecated must retain the PydanticDeprecatedSince210 notice.
pydantic/deprecated/decorator.py:ValidatedFunction.create_model prepares configuration first and then constructs ConfigWrapper with check=False, avoiding a second preparation pass.
proposed.applies: schema_generator deprecation handling and callers that prepare configuration before constructing ConfigWrapper.

proposed.title: Report overflowing ByteSize strings as validation errors
answers: Why does a very large byte-size string raise OverflowError?
How should ByteSize handle oversized values such as a 310-digit number followed by KB?
How do I preserve ByteSize validation errors when changing unit conversion?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Validating an extremely large byte-size string raises OverflowError instead of ValidationError.
Root cause: pydantic/types.py:ByteSize converts the numeric string to float, multiplies by the unit multiplier, and converts to int; this conversion can overflow.
Fix pattern: Catch OverflowError around the scaled numeric conversion and raise PydanticCustomError with code 'byte_size' and message 'could not parse value and unit from byte string'.
Constraints: This handling applies to overflow during numeric conversion with a recognized unit; unsupported units retain the separate 'byte_size_unit' error.
proposed.applies: ByteSize validation of numeric strings with byte units, especially values large enough to overflow float-to-int conversion.

proposed.title: Snapshot class namespaces before concurrent iteration
answers: Why does concurrent TypeAdapter construction fail while reading a class?
Why does creating models or dataclasses with a shared base race?
How should class namespaces be iterated in free-threaded builds?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Concurrent TypeAdapter construction, model/dataclass creation, or model rebuilding can fail because a class dictionary changes size during iteration.
Root cause: pydantic/_internal/_decorators.py:_decorator_infos_for_class and pydantic/_internal/_namespace_utils.py:LazyLocalNamespace.data iterate class namespaces that another thread can mutate by first reading annotations; Python 3.14 can add __annotations_cache__ or __annotate_func__.
Fix pattern: Iterate vars(typ).copy().items() when collecting decorators; copy MappingProxyType namespaces before iterating them when assembling lazy locals.
Constraints: This protects iteration over shared class namespaces during concurrent annotation access. LazyLocalNamespace.data copies only MappingProxyType inputs; other mappings retain their existing iteration behavior.
proposed.applies: Class namespace iteration during concurrent schema generation, decorator discovery, and annotation resolution.

proposed.title: Invalidate complete models with mocks during rebuilding
answers: Why can model instantiation race with model_rebuild(force=True)?
How should a forced rebuild invalidate validators and serializers?
Why must rebuild avoid deleting model schema attributes?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Instantiating a model concurrently with a forced rebuild can race with removal of its validation attributes.
Root cause: pydantic/main.py:BaseModel.model_rebuild previously deleted schema, validator, and serializer attributes; concurrent reads without the rebuild lock can then resolve attributes from a parent class.
Fix pattern: After marking the model incomplete, replace an already-complete model's schema, validator, and serializer with mocks through _mock_val_ser.set_model_mocks(cls), preventing reuse of the completed artifacts while keeping class attributes present.
Constraints: Reset mocks when already_complete is true. Incomplete models retain their existing mocks; completed schema, validator, and serializer artifacts must not be reused during rebuilding.
proposed.applies: Changes to BaseModel rebuilding and invalidation of compiled schema, validation, or serialization artifacts.

proposed.title: Exercise races with fresh shared state and synchronized workers
answers: How do I test concurrent TypeAdapter or model creation?
How do I reproduce a model rebuild race?
Why are the free-threading tests skipped?
proposed.body:
Use tests/test_freethreaded.py:run_concurrently(setup, target, *, rounds=100, threads=8) for concurrency regressions.
setup() creates fresh shared state each round; target(ctx, index) receives that state and a worker index, allowing one worker to rebuild while others instantiate or create subclasses.
A threading.Barrier releases all workers together, and future.result() propagates worker failures to the test.
The module skips tests on Emscripten and when tests/conftest.py:is_free_threaded is false; detection uses not sys._is_gil_enabled(), falling back to false when that API is absent.
For first-annotation-access races, setup must recreate the class each round so annotation caches from earlier rounds do not remove the triggering condition.
proposed.applies: Regression tests for shared-class races on Python runtimes running with the GIL disabled.

proposed.title: Defer mypy subclass processing until tagged model bases are ready
answers: Why does the mypy plugin crash with circular model imports?
Why are inherited fields missing from a model's constructor signature?
How should the mypy plugin handle an unfinished base model?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Mypy crashes with circular Pydantic model imports, and subclass constructor signatures can lose inherited fields.
Root cause: pydantic/mypy.py:PydanticModelTransformer.collect_fields_and_class_vars skips bases without completed METADATA_KEY metadata, even when their processing is pending because of unresolved forward references.
Fix pattern: pydantic/mypy.py:PydanticModelTransformer.transform tags models with METADATA_TAG_KEY before collecting fields; collection returns (None, None) for tagged, unfinished bases, and transform explicitly requests another pass with self._api.defer().
Constraints: Defer only before self._api.final_iteration. Missing METADATA_KEY alone does not justify deferral: untagged bases are still skipped. Preserve inherited fields before generating subclass signatures.
proposed.applies: Pydantic mypy plugin model transformation when inheritance and unresolved forward references require multiple semantic-analysis passes.

proposed.title: Gate temporal serialization formats on JSON schema mode
answers: Why does my validation schema say datetime is a number when ISO strings are accepted?
Should ser_json_temporal change the validation JSON schema?
Why does ser_json_timedelta='float' produce a numeric validation schema?
proposed.body:
Symptom: A temporal field's validation JSON schema declares a number even though the model accepts ISO 8601 strings.
Root cause: pydantic/json_schema.py:GenerateJsonSchema._common_temporal_schema consulted the serialization format without checking the schema mode.
Fix pattern: Require self.mode == 'serialization' before emitting a numeric schema for a non-ISO temporal serialization format.
Constraints: Applies to date, time, datetime and timedelta; validation schemas retain string types with their temporal formats. Serialization schemas still use numbers for seconds or milliseconds. val_temporal_unit controls numeric input interpretation and does not disable ISO string input.
proposed.applies: Temporal JSON schema generation under ser_json_temporal or ser_json_timedelta settings.

proposed.title: Preserve include/exclude when a custom serializer is skipped
answers: Why does model_dump ignore include or exclude with a JSON-only model serializer?
How should fallback serialization handle include/exclude?
When should function serializers clear filtering state?
proposed.body:
Symptom: model_dump() ignores include/exclude when a plain or wrap model serializer is configured with when_used='json' and skipped in Python mode.
Root cause: pydantic-core/src/serializers/type_serializers/function.rs:function_type_serializer cleared filtering state before fallback serialization even when self.call reported that the function was not invoked.
Fix pattern: Preserve current filters via pydantic-core/src/serializers/extra.rs:SerializationState::include_exclude for the fallback serializer; use empty filters for the return serializer when the function was invoked. Keep this branching consistent across to_python, json_key, and serde_serialize in function_type_serializer.
Constraints: Preserve filters only for the skipped-function fallback branch. When the function runs, filtering is treated as handled by that function, so include/exclude must not be reapplied to its returned value.
proposed.applies: Function serializer dispatch, including plain and wrap model serializers whose when_used condition can skip invocation.

proposed.title: GeneralFieldsSerializer GC traversal must include the extra serializer
answers: Which GeneralFieldsSerializer members must participate in GC traversal?
How does Python garbage collection reach the extra-field serializer?
Where should missing serializer GC traversal be fixed?
proposed.body:
Invariant: GeneralFieldsSerializer GC traversal must include fields, computed_fields, and extra_serializer.
Enforcement: pydantic-core/src/serializers/fields.rs:GeneralFieldsSerializer declares these members through impl_py_gc_traverse!.
Consequence: Omitting extra_serializer leaves the extra-field serializer outside this traversal.
Constraints: This rule covers GeneralFieldsSerializer; other serializer types require their own traversal definitions to be checked.
proposed.applies: Changes to GeneralFieldsSerializer members or its Python GC traversal implementation.

proposed.title: Resolve type-alias references for callable discriminators in both schema-generation paths
answers: Why does Field(discriminator=...) fail with a PEP 695 type alias?
How do callable discriminators find tags behind type-alias references?
Why does a callable discriminator work in Annotated but fail when supplied through Field?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Callable discriminators fail for tagged unions declared through PEP 695 type aliases when supplied via Field(discriminator=...).
Root cause: pydantic/_internal/_discriminated_union.py:apply_discriminator did not forward definitions, while pydantic/types.py:Discriminator._convert_schema resolved references only through a schema-generation handler.
Fix pattern: Pass the definitions registry into callable-discriminator conversion and share reference resolution between the root union and choices whose tag metadata is missing.
Constraints: In pydantic/types.py:Discriminator._convert_schema, use handler resolution when a handler is present, otherwise use the supplied definitions registry; an unresolved root reference must raise MissingDefinitionForUnionRef. Resolve a choice reference for tag lookup only when its tag is missing. This pattern concerns callable discriminators; string discriminators use the inferred-discriminator path.
proposed.applies: Callable discriminator schema conversion for unions or tagged choices represented by definition references, including PEP 695 type aliases used through Field.

proposed.title: Avoid double-wrapping polymorphic model serializers
answers: Why are polymorphic model serializers wrapped twice?
How should serializer construction return a resolved model serializer?
How do I avoid adding a second polymorphism trampoline?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Polymorphic model serializers are wrapped twice.
Root cause: The CombinedSerializer construction path called pydantic-core/src/serializers/shared.rs:CombinedSerializer::maybe_wrap_in_polymorphism_trampoline again after CombinedSerializer::find_serializer returned.
Fix pattern: Return CombinedSerializer::find_serializer's result directly from the final construction path instead of adding another trampoline wrapper.
Constraints: Applies to this final serializer-resolution path; the diff does not establish that trampoline wrapping should be removed from other paths.
proposed.applies: Final serializer resolution in CombinedSerializer when constructing polymorphic model serializers.

proposed.title: Compare SecretStr values as bytes to support all strings
answers: Why does comparing secrets containing non-ASCII characters raise TypeError?
How should SecretStr equality preserve constant-time comparison?
How can SecretStr equality support lone Unicode surrogates?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Comparing two SecretStr values containing non-ASCII text raises TypeError instead of returning an equality result.
Root cause: pydantic/types.py:SecretStr.__eq__ passed strings to secrets.compare_digest(), which accepts only ASCII string arguments.
Fix pattern: Encode both secret values as UTF-8 bytes with errors='surrogatepass' before calling secrets.compare_digest(); this preserves constant-time comparison and supports lone surrogates.
Constraints: Preserve the existing class check that returns False for incompatible operands. This encoding applies to SecretStr; SecretBytes already supplies bytes accepted by compare_digest().
proposed.applies: Changes to SecretStr equality, especially Unicode handling and constant-time comparison.

proposed.title: Unhashable generic arguments must bypass caching without breaking model creation
answers: Why does parameterizing a generic Pydantic model raise an unhashable TypeError?
Can a generic model use Annotated metadata with __hash__ = None?
How should the generic type cache handle unhashable type arguments?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Parameterizing a generic Pydantic model with unhashable Annotated metadata raises TypeError instead of producing a model that validates normally.
Root cause: pydantic/_internal/_generics.py:get_cached_generic_type_early, get_cached_generic_type_late and set_cached_generic_type accessed a cache whose keys can contain unhashable generic arguments.
Fix pattern: Route cache reads and writes through pydantic/_internal/_generics.py:_generic_cache_get and _generic_cache_set; handle TypeError from cache access as a cache miss or skipped write.
Constraints: Apply this fallback only around cache access, not model construction or validation. Preserve early and late cache entries, including the alternate early key for a single type argument, for hashable arguments.

proposed.title: Preserve zero-valued Interval bounds in pipeline validation
answers: Why does a pipeline Interval accept negative values despite ge=0?
Why does Interval(gt=0) allow zero?
How should pipeline validation handle zero bounds for ge, gt, le and lt?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Pipeline Interval validation silently accepts values outside a range when a bound is zero, including zero itself for an exclusive bound.
Root cause: pydantic/experimental/pipeline.py:_apply_constraint checked Interval bounds for truthiness, treating zero as absent.
Fix pattern: Check each bound with `is not None` before delegating to its Ge, Gt, Le or Lt constraint; cover zero bounds and boundary acceptance in tests/test_pipeline.py:test_interval_constraints.
Constraints: Applies to all four optional Interval bounds (ge, gt, le, lt); None means absent, while zero must retain the corresponding inclusive or exclusive comparison semantics.
proposed.applies: Interval bound decomposition in the experimental pipeline API and its regression tests.

proposed.title: Numeric datetime serialization must honor timezone offsets and preserve fractional seconds
answers: Why does serializing a timezone-aware datetime as seconds produce the wrong timestamp?
How should milliseconds serialization account for UTC offsets and microseconds?
Should datetime dictionary keys honor ser_json_temporal timezone offsets?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Serializing a timezone-aware datetime as seconds or milliseconds produces a timestamp that ignores its UTC offset.
Root cause: pydantic-core/src/serializers/type_serializers/datetime_etc.rs:datetime_to_seconds and datetime_to_milliseconds combined a date timestamp with local clock time, losing the timezone offset.
Fix pattern: Derive whole seconds from dt.timestamp_tz(), then add microseconds divided by 1_000_000 for seconds; for milliseconds, multiply whole seconds by 1_000 and add microseconds divided by 1_000.
Constraints: Applies to datetime JSON serialization with ser_json_temporal='seconds' or 'milliseconds', including dictionary keys. Preserve fractional precision and consistent values across JSON-mode Python output and JSON bytes; ordinary to_python retains the datetime, as checked by pydantic-core/tests/serializers/test_datetime.py:test_config_datetime_tz_aware. This pattern does not cover ISO formatting or date/time-only conversion.
proposed.applies: Timezone-aware datetime values and dictionary keys serialized using numeric temporal modes.
